clue.text: Rear stimulation gives a thrill to hacks briefly. Article? Pass

parts.note: a kick is a buzz of excitement
UP is the short form of United Press, a news agency feeding hacks, or journalists
the Khyber Pass, between Afghanistan and Pakistan

explanation.surface: A dispatch from the press, chopped into fragments, about a thrill and a famous mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: KHYBER is Cockney rhyming slang: Khyber Pass for arse, so a kick up the Khyber is a kick up the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick up the backside is the rear-end prod that jolts a slacker into action, here in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Chancellor, once Blair's flipped and kicked out Left "cabbages"

indicators.note: flipped as in turned over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for Left is booted out of the jumbled name

parts.note: the name with its possessive s

explanation.surface: A political jibe about an ex-chancellor and a Blair who has flipped and kicked out the Left as vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a turnip-like variety of cabbage, hence the quotation marks on the looser plural.

clue.text: Awfully nice to squeeze up pimple of Londoner?

indicators.note: the jumbled word squeezes the other piece into its middle
awfully suggests the word is mangled, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: zit is slang for a spot

explanation.surface: Squeezing a Londoner's spot is awfully nice, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a Londoner is one kind of city dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Any inhabitant of a city such as London is a citizen of it, so the Londoner is one example.

clue.text: Bush at heart accepts the point: past it and still on the shelf

indicators.note: the middle letters take the point inside them
the heart of a word is its middle, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: the word whose middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: George Bush, past it and accepting the point, is left on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods still on the shelf have found no buyer, which is exactly what remains when nothing has been sold.

clue.text: Having trouble giving a blow job, being a joker?

definitions.text: Having trouble giving a blow job

definitions.meaning: second meaning: making gags, telling jokes

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the throat's reflex, the other is a comedian's trade in gags.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is both to retch and to crack jokes, so the present participle covers both senses.

clue.text: Klosters entertainment "a pisser," snapped King coming in

indicators.note: the king's letter enters the jumbled phrase
snapped as in broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy king calls the ski-resort fun a pisser and snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Klosters is the Swiss ski resort favoured by British royalty, hence the King.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising and drinking at a resort after a day on the slopes, such as at Klosters.

clue.text: Piss off a wet involved in homosexual environment

indicators.note: the word for homosexual surrounds the other letters like an environment
involved as in convoluted, so these letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: A political wet, mixed up in a gay scene, is told where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: A wet is a moderate Tory of the Thatcher years.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive imperatives telling someone to leave; get away is the milder phrasing of the same order.

clue.text: Gets hands on dough, say … is not satisfied

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a baker kneads dough by working it with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone grabbing money still wants more.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough suggests money, but it is the baker's dough, worked with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who needs something lacks it, so their want is not yet met or satisfied.

clue.text: Put pipe down before sex goes on: life isn't a bed of roses

definitions.text: life isn't a bed of roses

indicators.note: the call for quiet comes first

explanation.surface: Someone is told to shut up before the sex starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The vulgar catchphrase is a shrug at misfortune: bad things occur, so life is no easy ride.

clue.text: Pledges to go in for bondage during foreign cruises

indicators.note: the binding sits in the middle of the jumbled word, as an event during a cruise
foreign suggests strange, so the letters are put in an outlandish order

explanation.surface: Kinky promises made on cruises abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Securities are guarantees or collateral given to back a loan, a formal kind of pledge.

clue.text: Conservative that hurt King Edward, the layabout

parts.note: ouch is what you say when something hurt
a King Edward is a common British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A Tory once wounded a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is an idle person who lounges in front of the TV, a modern idler.

clue.text: Liz dancing in her underwear — crazy, they're liable to get crushed

indicators.note: the letters of the name dance about into a new order

explanation.surface: Liz dances about in her underwear like a madwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: In here just means wearing: the jumbled name follows the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-shelled Brazil nuts have to be cracked open with nutcrackers, so they are made to be crushed.

clue.text: Privileged American giving head to William "the Snake"

indicators.note: the head of the name is its first letter

parts.note: the name whose first letter is used
an asp is a small venomous snake

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of William and a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: A WASP is a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, the old US establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names the upper-class white Protestant elite who traditionally ran American society.

clue.text: Potty character, name of Tony

parts.note: Ben of Bill and Ben the Flowerpot Men, an old BBC children's show

explanation.surface: A daft character called Tony.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Benn was the veteran Labour left-winger, so his surname stands for the first name.

clue.text: See 1
MI6's role given abnormal powers with no one up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means these letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: an age is a long period

explanation.surface: Spies given supernatural powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying for Britain abroad is the intelligence agency's job, so espionage is its function.

clue.text: Say, at the end of snog with singer Barry. "It's liable to get into a froth"?

definitions.text: It's liable to get into a froth

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used
Barry White, the deep-voiced soul singer

explanation.surface: A romantic snog with Barry White playing, which gets someone frothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten albumen whips into a stiff foam, as in meringue, so it readily turns frothy.

clue.text: London district gives Cyclops support for member, quite a heavyweight

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself, I
a sling holds up an injured arm, or limb
a ton is a huge weight

explanation.surface: The setter boasts about his support for a hefty politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Member looks like an MP, but it is an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of north London, famed for its well-heeled Labour residents.

clue.text: Ed once accepted sheep should get good stuffing

indicators.note: the letter for good is stuffed between the pieces

explanation.surface: An editor accepts that the sheep need decent stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Ingrams was the long-serving editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed is short for editor; Ingrams edited the magazine for over twenty years before stepping down.

clue.text: Nick, the Westminster bully-boy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to steal, in British slang
second meaning: a party official who enforces MPs' votes

explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name, but here it is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whip means to steal in slang and also names the parliamentary official who keeps members in line.

clue.text: See 9
Fly Tony's debut fixed for Home Counties

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used
the counties around London, in the south-east of England

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's first outing was arranged in the Home Counties.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness, a species of fly.

clue.text: Horny beast of a city type who's in and out quickly?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a male deer, with antlers

definitions.text: a city type who's in and out quickly?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a speculator who buys new shares to sell at once

explanation.walkthrough: Horny suggests lust, but it means bearing antlers; the City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an antlered male deer, and in the City a trader who flips new share issues for a quick profit.

clue.text: Loser's throw-away line after model duck weekend

indicators.note: the line comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A dirty weekend with a model where someone gets ditched.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's corner throws in the towel to concede, so it is what the losing side tosses away.

clue.text: Bunny's poser: was Dutch cap's end knotted without ring?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the ring
knotted as in tangled, so the letters are rearranged
only the end of the word is taken

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used
a ring is round like O

explanation.surface: Questions about a contraceptive cap's failure.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dutch cap is a diaphragm contraceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs Bunny's catchphrase is a question, so it is the rabbit's poser.

clue.text: Labour needs one dodgy ticket-seller to get through a bad time

parts.note: a tout resells tickets at inflated prices

explanation.surface: The Labour Party leans on a shady ticket tout to survive a bad patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the party but is plain toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat it out is an idiom for enduring an ordeal until it ends.

clue.text: Test drug flipped Clifford

indicators.note: the first name is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A drug test that sent the PR man Max Clifford into a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge, short for examination.

clue.text: Bully inserts length between tits on Brenda

indicators.note: the length is put inside the bust
the letter sits between the bust's letters

parts.note: Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A lecher shoves something between the Queen's breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluster is to rant and threaten in an overbearing way, as a bully does.

clue.text: Reportedly commits foul on Eastender in our underperforming football club

indicators.note: the pieces said aloud give the answer's sound

parts.note: a player who knees someone commits a foul; Den Watts was the landlord in the BBC soap EastEnders

explanation.surface: A footballer fouls a player from the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Neasden FC is Private Eye's running joke of a hopeless football team in a dull north London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine's fictional Neasden club always loses, so it is its own useless team.
